import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# --- Data Preparation ---

# Identify the top 10 most common primary breeds overall.
# We'll treat "Mischling" (Mixed Breed) as a distinct category.
top_breeds = df['Rasse1Text'].value_counts().nlargest(10).index

# Filter the dataframe to include only data for the top 10 breeds
df_top_breeds = df[df['Rasse1Text'].isin(top_breeds)].copy()

# Group by year and breed to get the annual count for each of the top breeds
breed_trends = df_top_breeds.groupby(['StichtagDatJahr', 'Rasse1Text']).size().reset_index(name='count')

# Get the actual year range for the title
min_year = breed_trends['StichtagDatJahr'].min()
max_year = breed_trends['StichtagDatJahr'].max()

# --- Visualization ---

# Set a modern and clean plot style
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Create the figure and axes
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 9))

# Create the line plot showing trends over time
sns.lineplot(
    data=breed_trends,
    x='StichtagDatJahr',
    y='count',
    hue='Rasse1Text',
    ax=ax,
    linewidth=2.5,
    palette='tab10',  # Colorblind-friendly palette for distinct categories
    marker='o',
    markersize=6,
    hue_order=top_breeds # Ensure legend order matches popularity
)

# --- Customization and Annotations ---

# Set a clear title and subtitle for context
fig.suptitle(f'Popularity Trends of Top 10 Dog Breeds in Zurich ({min_year}–{max_year})',
             fontsize=18, fontweight='bold', x=0.125, y=0.98, ha='left')
ax.set_title('Annual count of registered dogs shows consistent popularity for Chihuahuas, French Bulldogs, and mixed breeds.',
             fontsize=12, color='dimgray', loc='left', pad=10)


# Set informative axis labels
ax.set_xlabel('Year', fontsize=12, labelpad=15)
ax.set_ylabel('Number of Registered Dogs', fontsize=12, labelpad=15)

# Customize axis ticks for readability
ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mticker.MaxNLocator(integer=True))
plt.xticks(fontsize=11)
plt.yticks(fontsize=11)

# Improve the legend
# Move the legend outside the plot area to prevent overlap
handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
ax.legend(handles=handles, labels=labels, title='Dog Breed',
          bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0., fontsize=11, title_fontsize=13)

# Remove top and right spines for a cleaner look
sns.despine(ax=ax)

# Adjust layout to prevent labels from being cut off
fig.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.85, 0.95])

# Save the final figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
